A. Tibial Preparation
A1. Tibial Extra-medullary Alignment Method
The knee is placed in maximal flexion with a subluxated tibia that is anteriorly stabilised.
Assemble the Tibial EM Alignment Guide to the selected Tibial Cutting Jig. The surgeon may select this from available MIS
Left or right or standard 0, 3 or 5 degrees slope.
With the knee fully flexed, position the distal portion of the Tibial EM Alignment Guide at the anterior ankle joint with its
Supramalleolar spring tabs. Position the proximal portion of the Tibial EM alignment guide by impacting the spikes of the
Tibial EM Alignment Guide onto the central portion of the proximal tibial plateau. While aligning the tibial EM alignment
guide, ensure that it aligns with patient's 2nd toe (of operating leg). At this time, confirm parallel alignment of the tibial
cutting guide to the mechanical axis in both coronal & sagittal planes. Use the fine adjustment knob at the proximal end of
the tibial cutting guide to make finer adjustments to the desired bone resection level.
Important Note: the tibial stylus can be used to measure the bone resection level, the stylus can be adjusted to different
resection levels from 0- 13mm and depending on patient's anatomy, the operating surgeon has option to choose tibial
resection level. The tip of stylus should be positioned on the lowest point on tibial plateau.

A2. Tibial Cutting Jig Positioning and Tibial Resection
Once the desired resection level is achieved, 2 long headless pins can be drilled into square holes marked zero to secure
the tibial resection guide. Additional pins may also be drilled to secure the guide during tibial resection.
Once the Tibial Cutting guide is securely positioned, Tibial EM Alignment Guide is now removed by disengaging the spike
using a Tibial EM Guide Extractor. Resection of the tibial plateau is now performed by using a 1.24 mm oscillating saw
blade.
Important Note: Prior to resection, if the surgeon wishes to increase or decrease the tibial resection thickness the "+2" or
"-2" hole are to be utilized to reposition the Tibial Cutting Jig.
MF-BBXX02A-16

B. Femoral Preparation
B1. Preparing Femoral Pilot Hole
With the ACL removed, the typical femoral entry point is slightly medial to the center of the intercondylar notch and
approximately 5-7 mm anterior to the anterior insertion of the PCL into the femur.
Important note: As both varus and valgus deformities are commonly encountered in the total knee patient, cautious
evaluation of the possible AP and ML curvature of the femoral shaft should be undertaken to consider shifting the initial
entry hole to a more appropriate location for each specific patient.
A surgical marker is used to mark the hole location; followed by an 8 mm step Drill to create an opening in the femoral
canal. The drill is typically inserted to a depth of approximately 100 mm within the femoral canal. Ensure that the drill is
parallel to the shaft of femur in both AP & lateral projections.
After removal of the drill, intra-medullary fluid along with bone debris may be flushed out of femur to avoid any fat
embolism.
4

B2. Femoral Valgus Angle Confirmation
Once an access to the canal is created, adjust the locating device (range± 10degree) to the pre-operatively estimated
valgus angle and load it on the appropriate length of the Femoral IM Rod (with T-Handle) manually insert the Femoral IM
Rod into the femoral canal. Fix the locating device on the femur with spike to ensure that the device is in firm contact with
the distal femur. Important note: Use a long IM rod (40cm) for tall patients or a small IM rod (30cm) for average height
patients.
B3. Distal Femur Bone Besection
Adjust the out trigger to desired distal femur cut level (the standard suggested distal femur cut is 9mm) and attach the
distal femur cutting jig to the out trigger. Connect this assembly to the locating device.
To secure the DFCG firmly to anterior femur, drill non-headed long pins in the square marked zero holes. Once the entire
instrument assembly is secured, the angel wing is used to assess the depth of distal femur cut and if necessary
appropriate adjustments are recommended to adjust the DFCG to pre-operative desired level. Press the hook available
on out trigger to release the DFCG jig from entire assembly by pulling the IM rod using T handle leaving behind only the
DFCG fixed with pins.

Important Note: +-2 mm guide holes on the DFCG provides options to allow additional resection if desired. Once the
distal femur resection is assessed and adjusted to desired level, distal femur resection is performed through the cutting
slot using a 25mm wide oscillating saw blade with 1.24mm thickness..

C. Extension and Flexion Gap Confirmation
The flexion and extension joint space gaps may be evaluated at this time with the spacer block (the 9mm spacer block
initially selected) to assess both the flexion and extension joint space.
If a thicker gap is observed, try additional spacer block (available in 11, 14 & 17mm) with different thickness and test
again for rectangular extension gap. If the extension gap is trapezoidal, soft tissues must be balanced to achieve
rectangular space.
A set of spacer blocks measures the gap and indicates the appropriate thickness of tibial insert.
(subject to re-evaluation at the time of trial reduction)
If neither the flexion and extension gaps nor soft tissue tension shows any problem, insert the femoral and tibial
provisional to test the knee mobility and their relative position.
Important Note: The flexion gap can also be measured before & after the 5 distal femur cuts with 5-in-1 cutting guide
in-situ. Use of 6mm or 8mm is recommended at this stage for checking 9mm or 11mm flexion gap.
The alignment rod is inserted through the spacer block handle to assess the extra-medullary alignment in both flexion
and extension.

D. Femoral component sizing
Extract the non-headed long pins using pin extractor instrument and remove the DFC G after distal femur resection. Take
the AP sizing guide and fix the distal part depending upon the size of femur.
Important Note: Use the 'LARGE' marked distal component of AP sizing guide for bigger bones and 'SMALL' marked one
for smaller bones)
Orient the AP sizing guide to desired side of knee being operated upon by rotating it. Place the AP sizing guide flush
against the resected distal femur with its two saddles rested flat against the posterior femoral condyles and ensure its
stylus touches the lowest point of the lateral anterior femoral cortex to avoid any potential notching of femur. The
estimated size is indicated on the front of AP sizing guide and tighten the screw to ascertain the correct size of femur.

Important Note: The AP sizing guide is reversible instrument, which allows for sizing of either right or left femur based on
the orientation of the sizer.
Important Note: The Freedom Knee system is anterior referencing system. In case the estimated size lies in between two
sizes, it is recommended to choose the smaller/lower size. Any additional bone resection will be removed from posterior
condyles. Under-sizing causes looseness in flexion and possible notching of anterior femoral cortex while over-sizing
causes tightness in flexion and increased tension in quadriceps mechanism.
To establish the external rotation, drill the non-headed long pins in desired holes, the AP sizing guide has 2 holes each for 3
degree and 6 degree external rotation. In case desired external rotation is 3 degree, drill pins in 3 degree holes, drill both
the pins in 6 degree holes to achieve 6 degree external rotation. There is additional option of achieving 4.5 degree
external rotation by placing one pin in 3 degree hole and other pin in six degree hole.

E. 5-in-1 Femur Resection
Remove the AP sizing guide leaving the long non-headed pins in place & position the estimated size of 5-in-1 cutting guide
as determined by the AP sizing guide, on the predrilled pins on distal femur by sliding on pins through rectangular slot.
Important Note: The 5-in-1 cutting guide should be flush seated on the distal femur.
At this step, there is the option of reconfirming the estimated size again by attaching optional stylus to the 5-in-1 cutting
guide and ensure its stylus touches the lowest point of the lateral anterior femoral cortex.
Drill lug screws in peg holes of 5-in-1 guide using power system to flush seat them completely. Use additional cancellous
pins in lateral & medial holes to enhance stability during resection and check resection thickness using angel wing in
anterior and posterior resection slots. Next, complete the Anterior, posterior, Anterior Chamfer and Posterior chamfer
resections using a 25mm wide oscillating saw blade with 1.24mm thickness through appropriate slots in 5-in-1 cutting
guide. Use 10mm wide reciprocating saw blade with 1.24mm thickness to complete the trochlear groove resection using
the trochlear grove slot in 5-in-1 cutting guide.

Important Note: The width of 5-in-1 cutting guide matches with the corresponding Freedom Femoral component. (Except
for size A)
Important Note: If positioned in external rotation correctly on the distal face of the femur, then, more of posterior medial
femoral condyle would be resected compare to posterior lateral femoral condyle. Be careful not to transect the
attachment of the medial collateral ligament (MCL) during the resection of posterior condyles. To reassess the flexion gap,
flex the knee at 90 degree and insert the 9mm or 11mm spacer blocks with alignment rod.
At this point the femoral resection for cruciate retaining femoral component is complete.

F. Femoral Notch/Box Cut (For Freedom PS design knee only)
Flex the knee at 90 degree and secure the femoral Notch/Box cut guide to the distal femur with two short headed pins.
Use a reciprocating saw to cut the sides and base of inter-condylar box while protecting tibia. A visual clearance of
complete clearance of resected bone is advised.
G. Trial with Tibial Base Plate Provisional
Try the different tibial Base Plate provisional options available from size 1 to 8 on the resected tibial surface; select the
one which offers maximum bone coverage in ML of resected tibia, without any implant overhang to obtain the
desired tibial tray size.
Important Note: Check the rotation and alignment using the alignment rod (through the hole on the tibial space
measure handle).

H. Creating Keel Space for Tibial Base Plate
Fix the desired Tibial Base plate provisional on the tibia with short headed pins. Attach the Tibial broach housing to it
and ream gently an opening with the 17mm Tibial reamer until the STOP on the reamer reaches the top of the tibial
broach housing. The 17mm reamer creates space for a 30mm Keel. Select the appropriate Tibial broach (use tibial
metal back broach for metal backed tibia & the all poly broach for all poly tibia) and attach it to slap hammer.
Position the Tibial broach to the guide hole on the Tibial Base plate provisional and ensure that the broach hits
precisely and vertically into the tibial canal creating space for the wings of tibia base plate.
Remove all the instruments leaving behind the tibial tray provisional for further trial reduction. Insert the Keel stabilizer
in the space created in the tibial tray provisional with appropriate size of provisional insert. Now, the tibia is ready for a
trial reduction.

I. Final Trial Reduction Preparation
11. Femoral Provisional Insertion
Assemble the CR/PS femoral provisional to the femoral Impactor-Extractor. Cautiously introduce femoral provisional
on the prepared femoral surface aligning the peg holes with pegs on the femoral provisional and perform gentle
impactions with the femoral impactor till the femoral provisional sits flush on the resected femoral surface.
12. Tibial base plate Provisional insertion
As the freedom knee system allows inter-changeability of femoral and tibial implant sizes select the Tibial base plate
provisional that best provides maximum coverage of the proximal tibia.
Once selected, attach the tibial base plate provisional with Keel stabilizer in it, to the handle and reposition this assembly
onto the tibia. The alignment rod may be inserted into the tibial base plate provisional handle to further evaluate the
positioning of the tibial base plate provisional. Remove the tibial base plate provisional handle and insert a CR/PS tibial
insert provisional of desired thickness.

J. Patella Preparation
J1. Patellar Resection Measurement
Evert the patella and remove excessive osteophytes. With a calliper, measure and record the thickness of the
anterior - posterior dimension of the patella.
Important Note: To plan the resection thickness, it is recommended to retain a 14 mm minimum thickness of patella
bone to support the implant structure. By 'Overstuffing' the patella, femoral joint can lead to flexion loss while
leaving a thin patella can lead to fracture or early loosening of patella.
J2. Patellar Resection
The patellar resection guide is used to determine the desired patellar diameter and position. Typically the guide is
positioned over the highest point of the articulation and the centre position is marked with an electrocautery or
surgical marker. Once the patella surface is resected, use the corresponding patella drill guide to assess the size of
patella. Using the 'patella peg drill' guide drill 3 holes in remaining patella bone. Place the patella provisional on to
the resurfaced patella and begin range of motion evaluation of patellar tracking.

K. Implant Preparation
K1. Bone Cement Preparation
After satisfactory final trial reduction, remove all provisional and clean the resected bones of all tissue debris.
Using the standard mixing protocol for the bone cement, mix and prepare the bone cement for cementing the implants.
K2. Cementing & Fixing Implants
Prior to cementing, irrigate the bone surfaces and drill sclerotic areas with a 1/8" drill bit to a depth of approximately
1/8". Firmly press bone cement into the bone surfaces, including the reamed keel entry hole to allow for adequate
indigitation. Place bone cement on the under surface of tibial definitive implant and firmly impact it on the prepared
tibia using the tibial impactor. Remove access bone cement.
Hyperflex the knee and dry the distal femoral bone cuts. Finger pressurise the posterior condyles with the bone cement.
Apply the bone cement to the under surface of the femoral component. Firmly impact the femoral component into place
using femoral impactor. Remove access bone cement.
If the metal backed tibial tray is being used, irrigate the surface of the tray and remove any access debris to clear the
locking mechanism. Firmly impact the selected articular surface liner into place and check to see that the locking
mechanism is engaged.
Reduce the knee and place it into extension. Evert the patella, dry the bony surface of patella and place bone cement
into the bone surface, apply bone cement underneath the patella implant. Place the patella implant on the resected
bone. Use patella pressuriser clamp to secure the patella implant. Trim access osteophytes and remove access bone
cement.

full_raw_transcription:
MonoMod™ Revision Femoral Stem System.
- World's First Monobloc-Modular: Combines monobloc structural integrity (zero breakage risk) with modular-like balancing capabilities.
- Design: Tapered Fluted Titanium (TFT); 2.5° taper geometry for enhanced zone of scratch fixation; 8-10 longitudinal ribs for rotational resistance.
- Shoulder Height Level (SHL): Unique technical concept for precise matching of reamer seating to definitive prosthesis, making modularity redundant.
- 3D Printed Augments: Highly porous proximal femoral augments to prevent subsidence and unitize trochanteric fragments.
- Material: Forged Titanium Alloy (Ti-6Al-4V-ELI); beveled tip to accommodate femoral bow.
salient_features: Monobloc-Modular Hybrid Design
3D Printed Porous Augments
Shoulder Height Level (SHL)
Fluted TFT Geometry

Bi-Level Positive Airway Pressure Device
Product Overview
The Meril BreathFlex™™ BPAP Device is an advanced non-invasive ventilation system engineered to support patients
with obstructive, central, or mixed sleep apnea, as well as conditions causing hypoventilation.
It delivers two distinct pressure levels - IPAP (Inhalation Pressure) and EPAP (Exhalation Pressure) - to maintain airway
patency while allowing natural exhalation comfort. This system is designed for both home and hospital use, combining
clinical accuracy with patient comfort.
A sophisticated algorithm powered by PneumaLogic™™ technology continuously monitors and identifies Central Sleep
Apnea (CSA) events, safeguarding patients against clinically inappropriate pressure adjustments.
The device's AdaptivelQ™™ technology intelligently automates the entire therapy process by continuously monitoring
breathing patterns to detect and classify respiratory events, dynamically adjusting pressure and airflow in real time to
compensate for leaks and deliver optimal treatment, and seamlessly switching between APAP and CPAP modes
without any manual intervention

Ureteral Balloon Dilatation Catheter: Dual markers for precise balloon positioning. Rapid inflation/deflation. Pebax Material.
Size Matrix: 4 FR (60mm/850mm), 4 FR (60mm/650mm), 5 FR.
Use: Dilates ureteral strictures or prepares ureter for procedures.

Suprapubic Cystostomy Catheter: Chrysanthemum tip design prevents slip. Handle design for easy grip. Silicone remains soft at body temperature.
Use: Provides bladder drainage via percutaneous malecot catheter placement.

General-Purpose Ureteral Catheter: Soft PVC for flexibility. Tapered tip reduces trauma.
Use: Smooth navigation and precise contrast delivery.

Urinary Stone Retrieval Basket (Flexible & Rigid): Shape-memory design returns to original shape. Tipless basket reduces trauma. Nitinol wires. PI core for rotation control.

Size (Rigid): 4.5 FR, Length: 55cm.
Use: Removes urinary stones during endoscopic procedures.

Urological Retrieval Coil: Secure extraction of stone pieces. Resists holmium laser energy. 3 FR x 15cm.
Use: Capture and remove urinary tract stones and objects.

Ureteral Access Sheath: Hydrophilic coating. Multiple scope entries without re-dilation. Lumen integrity.
Size Matrix: 9/11 FR, 10/12 FR, 9.5/11.5 FR, 10.5/12.5 FR, 12/14 FR. Lengths: 26cm, 35cm, 45cm.
Y-Type & YB Bend Sheaths: Continuous irrigation, simultaneous scope access and suction. 13/15 FR x 46cm available.

Amplatz Sheath: Tapered distal end for smooth advancement. Kink-resistant PTFE material.

features_list: Primary stent platform for Metafor™ SES is NexGen™™ Cobalt Chromium Coronary Stent System.

It is known that Sirolimus inhibits T-lymphocyte activation and smooth muscle and endothelial cell proliferation in response to cytokine and growth factor stimulation.

In cells, sirolimus binds to the immunophilin, FK Binding Protein-12 (FKBP-12). The sirolimus-FKBP 12 complex binds to and inhibits the activation of the mammalian Target of Rapamycin (mTOR), leading to inhibition of cell cycle progression from the G1 to the S phase.

Product Overview
The Meril BreathFlex™™ BPAP Device is an advanced non-invasive ventilation system engineered to support patients
with obstructive, central, or mixed sleep apnea, as well as conditions causing hypoventilation.
It delivers two distinct pressure levels - IPAP (Inhalation Pressure) and EPAP (Exhalation Pressure) - to maintain airway
patency while allowing natural exhalation comfort. This system is designed for both home and hospital use, combining
clinical accuracy with patient comfort.
A sophisticated algorithm powered by PneumaLogic™™ technology continuously monitors and identifies Central Sleep
Apnea (CSA) events, safeguarding patients against clinically inappropriate pressure adjustments.
The device's AdaptivelQ™™ technology intelligently automates the entire therapy process by continuously monitoring
breathing patterns to detect and classify respiratory events, dynamically adjusting pressure and airflow in real time to
compensate for leaks and deliver optimal treatment, and seamlessly switching between APAP and CPAP modes
without any manual intervention
Key Features
Gentle, Adaptive Comfort
Dual-level pressure therapy reduces the work of breathing and improves sleep quality.
- Integrated heated humidifier (Levels 0-5) prevents dryness of nasal passages and throat.

BreathFlex™™ algorithm ensures smooth transition between inhalation and exhalation.

Product Overview
The Meril BreathFlex™™ BPAP Device is an advanced non-invasive ventilation system engineered to support patients
with obstructive, central, or mixed sleep apnea, as well as conditions causing hypoventilation.
It delivers two distinct pressure levels - IPAP (Inhalation Pressure) and EPAP (Exhalation Pressure) - to maintain airway
patency while allowing natural exhalation comfort. This system is designed for both home and hospital use, combining
clinical accuracy with patient comfort.
A sophisticated algorithm powered by PneumaLogic™™ technology continuously monitors and identifies Central Sleep
Apnea (CSA) events, safeguarding patients against clinically inappropriate pressure adjustments.
The device's AdaptivelQ™™ technology intelligently automates the entire therapy process by continuously monitoring
breathing patterns to detect and classify respiratory events, dynamically adjusting pressure and airflow in real time to
compensate for leaks and deliver optimal treatment, and seamlessly switching between APAP and CPAP modes
without any manual intervention
Key Features
Gentle, Adaptive Comfort
Dual-level pressure therapy reduces the work of breathing and improves sleep quality.
- Integrated heated humidifier (Levels 0-5) prevents dryness of nasal passages and throat.
Optional heated tubing (10 °C -30 °C) ensures consistent warmth in cooler environments.
BreathFlex™™ algorithm ensures smooth transition between inhalation and exhalation.
Smart Interface & Usability
Rotary-press control knob with intuitive on-screen navigation.
- Digital LCD display showing pressure curves, airflow data, and session time.
Auto-Start / Auto-Off mode starts when mask is worn, stops automatically 15 s after mask removal.

- Daily refill and cleaning recommended for hygiene and performance.

- Power-failure buzzer alert (≥ 15 s) ensures user awareness.

Internal evidence clearly identifies this as a 2 gm slab of refined natural beeswax, ivory white, sterilized by gamma radiation, non-absorbable with waxy odor. Common use cases include sternotomy, craniotomy, spinal surgery, and orthopedic procedures. Entity type is consumable (single-use, non-implantable). No conflicts detected. Pre-Operative Planning
As a standard protocol, a thorough physical examination of the knee should be performed to evaluate the patient's overall
knee function. Functional stability, muscle tone, ligamentous/ capsular laxity and/or contractures and potential bone
loss- all need to be considered during this step.
AP and Lateral standing radiographs alongwith a Skyline view in a known magnification should be obtained and
evaluated. Radiographs of the non-operative limb may also be considered to provide an additional reference.
Additionally, the surgeon may elect to obtain AP whole leg radiographs for both limbs to determine the current
hip/knee/ankle centres, anatomical & mechanical axis to allow for additional pre-operative planning of the intended
corrective osteotomies and resultant alignment/implant positioning.
If intra-medullary alignment instrumentation is intended for use, the shape and diameter of femoral and tibial canals
should be evaluated to help assure its successful use and the passage of intra-medullary alignment devices into respective
bone canals.
The intended implant size must also be evaluated on both AP and lateral radiographs by using the Meril Radiographic
overlay templates. The magnification percentage of the templates used should approximate the known magnification of
the radiographs.
Patient Preparation
The extremity to be operated is appropriately prepared and draped before applying tourniquet following application of
an Esmarch Bandage and inflated.

Surgical Incision
Freedom knee Instruments are designed for use with the traditional surgical methods and also for minimal invasive
techniques.
Three common used methods for surgical incision are:
•
Medial Parapatellar Approach
Sub Vastas Approach
•
Mid Vastas Approach
The surgeon may select either of these standard exposure methods to perform skin and capsular incision. If the medial
parapatellar approach is selected, a straight midline skin incision, extending above and below the patella is applied to
begin the exposure. The capsular exposure is then approached by utilizing a longitudinal medial parapatellar incision,
typically extending upward to a level of one third of the rectus femoris or vastus medialis and downward to the medial
side of the origin of patellar tendon on the tibial tuberosity.
Once the exposure is completed, the patella is everted in a standard fashion, and the knee joint is inspected. Cautious
assessment and removal of the osteophytes should be undertaken. ROM, patellar tracking and soft tissue
stability/instability should be evaluated again. It may be the preference of the surgeon to conduct a preliminary soft tissue
release of the fixed contracted structures. Once completed, the knee is flexed to 90 degrees to perform the initial femoral
pilot hole for the intra-medullary alignment.

A. Tibial Preparation
A1. Tibial Extra-medullary Alignment Method
The knee is placed in maximal flexion with a subluxated tibia that is anteriorly stabilised.
Assemble the Tibial EM Alignment Guide to the selected Tibial Cutting Jig. The surgeon may select this from available MIS
Left or right or standard 0, 3 or 5 degrees slope.
With the knee fully flexed, position the distal portion of the Tibial EM Alignment Guide at the anterior ankle joint with its
Supramalleolar spring tabs. Position the proximal portion of the Tibial EM alignment guide by impacting the spikes of the
Tibial EM Alignment Guide onto the central portion of the proximal tibial plateau. While aligning the tibial EM alignment
guide, ensure that it aligns with patient's 2nd toe (of operating leg). At this time, confirm parallel alignment of the tibial
cutting guide to the mechanical axis in both coronal & sagittal planes. Use the fine adjustment knob at the proximal end of
the tibial cutting guide to make finer adjustments to the desired bone resection level.
Important Note: the tibial stylus can be used to measure the bone resection level, the stylus can be adjusted to different
resection levels from 0- 13mm and depending on patient's anatomy, the operating surgeon has option to choose tibial
resection level. The tip of stylus should be positioned on the lowest point on tibial plateau.
FRE

A2. Tibial Cutting Jig Positioning and Tibial Resection
Once the desired resection level is achieved, 2 long headless pins can be drilled into square holes marked zero to secure
the tibial resection guide. Additional pins may also be drilled to secure the guide during tibial resection.
Once the Tibial Cutting guide is securely positioned, Tibial EM Alignment Guide is now removed by disengaging the spike
using a Tibial EM Guide Extractor. Resection of the tibial plateau is now performed by using a 1.24 mm oscillating saw
blade.
Important Note: Prior to resection, if the surgeon wishes to increase or decrease the tibial resection thickness the "+2" or
"-2" hole are to be utilized to reposition the Tibial Cutting Jig.
MF-BBXX02A-16
AA170702008 032
B. Femoral Preparation
B1. Preparing Femoral Pilot Hole
With the ACL removed, the typical femoral entry point is slightly medial to the center of the intercondylar notch and
approximately 5-7 mm anterior to the anterior insertion of the PCL into the femur.
Important note: As both varus and valgus deformities are commonly encountered in the total knee patient, cautious
evaluation of the possible AP and ML curvature of the femoral shaft should be undertaken to consider shifting the initial
entry hole to a more appropriate location for each specific patient.
A surgical marker is used to mark the hole location; followed by an 8 mm step Drill to create an opening in the femoral
canal. The drill is typically inserted to a depth of approximately 100 mm within the femoral canal. Ensure that the drill is
parallel to the shaft of femur in both AP & lateral projections.
After removal of the drill, intra-medullary fluid along with bone debris may be flushed out of femur to avoid any fat
embolism.
4
FREEDOM®
KNEE
B2. Femoral Valgus Angle Confirmation
Once an access to the canal is created, adjust the locating device (range± 10degree) to the pre-operatively estimated
valgus angle and load it on the appropriate length of the Femoral IM Rod (with T-Handle) manually insert the Femoral IM
Rod into the femoral canal. Fix the locating device on the femur with spike to ensure that the device is in firm contact with
the distal femur. Important note: Use a long IM rod (40cm) for tall patients or a small IM rod (30cm) for average height
patients.
B3. Distal Femur Bone Besection
Adjust the out trigger to desired distal femur cut level (the standard suggested distal femur cut is 9mm) and attach the
distal femur cutting jig to the out trigger. Connect this assembly to the locating device.
To secure the DFCG firmly to anterior femur, drill non-headed long pins in the square marked zero holes. Once the entire
instrument assembly is secured, the angel wing is used to assess the depth of distal femur cut and if necessary
appropriate adjustments are recommended to adjust the DFCG to pre-operative desired level. Press the hook available
on out trigger to release the DFCG jig from entire assembly by pulling the IM rod using T handle leaving behind only the
DFCG fixed with pins.

FREEDOM
Important Note: +-2 mm guide holes on the DFCG provides options to allow additional resection if desired. Once the
distal femur resection is assessed and adjusted to desired level, distal femur resection is performed through the cutting
slot using a 25mm wide oscillating saw blade with 1.24mm thickness..

C. Extension and Flexion Gap Confirmation
The flexion and extension joint space gaps may be evaluated at this time with the spacer block (the 9mm spacer block
initially selected) to assess both the flexion and extension joint space.
If a thicker gap is observed, try additional spacer block (available in 11, 14 & 17mm) with different thickness and test
again for rectangular extension gap. If the extension gap is trapezoidal, soft tissues must be balanced to achieve
rectangular space.
A set of spacer blocks measures the gap and indicates the appropriate thickness of tibial insert.
(subject to re-evaluation at the time of trial reduction)
If neither the flexion and extension gaps nor soft tissue tension shows any problem, insert the femoral and tibial
provisional to test the knee mobility and their relative position.
Important Note: The flexion gap can also be measured before & after the 5 distal femur cuts with 5-in-1 cutting guide
in-situ. Use of 6mm or 8mm is recommended at this stage for checking 9mm or 11mm flexion gap.
The alignment rod is inserted through the spacer block handle to assess the extra-medullary alignment in both flexion
and extension.
Extension and Flexion Gap Confirmation

D. Femoral component sizing
Extract the non-headed long pins using pin extractor instrument and remove the DFC G after distal femur resection. Take
the AP sizing guide and fix the distal part depending upon the size of femur.
Important Note: Use the 'LARGE' marked distal component of AP sizing guide for bigger bones and 'SMALL' marked one
for smaller bones)
Orient the AP sizing guide to desired side of knee being operated upon by rotating it. Place the AP sizing guide flush
against the resected distal femur with its two saddles rested flat against the posterior femoral condyles and ensure its
stylus touches the lowest point of the lateral anterior femoral cortex to avoid any potential notching of femur. The
estimated size is indicated on the front of AP sizing guide and tighten the screw to ascertain the correct size of femur.

LEFT

Important Note: The AP sizing guide is reversible instrument, which allows for sizing of either right or left femur based on
the orientation of the sizer.
Important Note: The Freedom Knee system is anterior referencing system. In case the estimated size lies in between two
sizes, it is recommended to choose the smaller/lower size. Any additional bone resection will be removed from posterior
condyles. Under-sizing causes looseness in flexion and possible notching of anterior femoral cortex while over-sizing
causes tightness in flexion and increased tension in quadriceps mechanism.
To establish the external rotation, drill the non-headed long pins in desired holes, the AP sizing guide has 2 holes each for 3
degree and 6 degree external rotation. In case desired external rotation is 3 degree, drill pins in 3 degree holes, drill both
the pins in 6 degree holes to achieve 6 degree external rotation. There is additional option of achieving 4.5 degree
external rotation by placing one pin in 3 degree hole and other pin in six degree hole.

E. 5-in-1 Femur Resection
Remove the AP sizing guide leaving the long non-headed pins in place & position the estimated size of 5-in-1 cutting guide
as determined by the AP sizing guide, on the predrilled pins on distal femur by sliding on pins through rectangular slot.
Important Note: The 5-in-1 cutting guide should be flush seated on the distal femur.
At this step, there is the option of reconfirming the estimated size again by attaching optional stylus to the 5-in-1 cutting
guide and ensure its stylus touches the lowest point of the lateral anterior femoral cortex.
Drill lug screws in peg holes of 5-in-1 guide using power system to flush seat them completely. Use additional cancellous
pins in lateral & medial holes to enhance stability during resection and check resection thickness using angel wing in
anterior and posterior resection slots. Next, complete the Anterior, posterior, Anterior Chamfer and Posterior chamfer
resections using a 25mm wide oscillating saw blade with 1.24mm thickness through appropriate slots in 5-in-1 cutting
guide. Use 10mm wide reciprocating saw blade with 1.24mm thickness to complete the trochlear groove resection using
the trochlear grove slot in 5-in-1 cutting guide.
G
FREEDOM
Important Note: The width of 5-in-1 cutting guide matches with the corresponding Freedom Femoral component. (Except
for size A)
Important Note: If positioned in external rotation correctly on the distal face of the femur, then, more of posterior medial
femoral condyle would be resected compare to posterior lateral femoral condyle. Be careful not to transect the
attachment of the medial collateral ligament (MCL) during the resection of posterior condyles. To reassess the flexion gap,
flex the knee at 90 degree and insert the 9mm or 11mm spacer blocks with alignment rod.
At this point the femoral resection for cruciate retaining femoral component is complete.

F. Femoral Notch/Box Cut (For Freedom PS design knee only)
Flex the knee at 90 degree and secure the femoral Notch/Box cut guide to the distal femur with two short headed pins.
Use a reciprocating saw to cut the sides and base of inter-condylar box while protecting tibia. A visual clearance of
complete clearance of resected bone is advised.
G. Trial with Tibial Base Plate Provisional
Try the different tibial Base Plate provisional options available from size 1 to 8 on the resected tibial surface; select the
one which offers maximum bone coverage in ML of resected tibia, without any implant overhang to obtain the
desired tibial tray size.
Important Note: Check the rotation and alignment using the alignment rod (through the hole on the tibial space
measure handle).

H. Creating Keel Space for Tibial Base Plate
Fix the desired Tibial Base plate provisional on the tibia with short headed pins. Attach the Tibial broach housing to it
and ream gently an opening with the 17mm Tibial reamer until the STOP on the reamer reaches the top of the tibial
broach housing. The 17mm reamer creates space for a 30mm Keel. Select the appropriate Tibial broach (use tibial
metal back broach for metal backed tibia & the all poly broach for all poly tibia) and attach it to slap hammer.
Position the Tibial broach to the guide hole on the Tibial Base plate provisional and ensure that the broach hits
precisely and vertically into the tibial canal creating space for the wings of tibia base plate.
Remove all the instruments leaving behind the tibial tray provisional for further trial reduction. Insert the Keel stabilizer
in the space created in the tibial tray provisional with appropriate size of provisional insert. Now, the tibia is ready for a
trial reduction.

I. Final Trial Reduction Preparation
11. Femoral Provisional Insertion
Assemble the CR/PS femoral provisional to the femoral Impactor-Extractor. Cautiously introduce femoral provisional
on the prepared femoral surface aligning the peg holes with pegs on the femoral provisional and perform gentle
impactions with the femoral impactor till the femoral provisional sits flush on the resected femoral surface.
12. Tibial base plate Provisional insertion
As the freedom knee system allows inter-changeability of femoral and tibial implant sizes select the Tibial base plate
provisional that best provides maximum coverage of the proximal tibia.
Once selected, attach the tibial base plate provisional with Keel stabilizer in it, to the handle and reposition this assembly
onto the tibia. The alignment rod may be inserted into the tibial base plate provisional handle to further evaluate the
positioning of the tibial base plate provisional. Remove the tibial base plate provisional handle and insert a CR/PS tibial
insert provisional of desired thickness.

J. Patella Preparation
J1. Patellar Resection Measurement
Evert the patella and remove excessive osteophytes. With a calliper, measure and record the thickness of the
anterior - posterior dimension of the patella.
Important Note: To plan the resection thickness, it is recommended to retain a 14 mm minimum thickness of patella
bone to support the implant structure. By 'Overstuffing' the patella, femoral joint can lead to flexion loss while
leaving a thin patella can lead to fracture or early loosening of patella.
J2. Patellar Resection
The patellar resection guide is used to determine the desired patellar diameter and position. Typically the guide is
positioned over the highest point of the articulation and the centre position is marked with an electrocautery or
surgical marker. Once the patella surface is resected, use the corresponding patella drill guide to assess the size of
patella. Using the 'patella peg drill' guide drill 3 holes in remaining patella bone. Place the patella provisional on to
the resurfaced patella and begin range of motion evaluation of patellar tracking.

K. Implant Preparation
K1. Bone Cement Preparation
After satisfactory final trial reduction, remove all provisional and clean the resected bones of all tissue debris.
Using the standard mixing protocol for the bone cement, mix and prepare the bone cement for cementing the implants.
K2. Cementing & Fixing Implants
Prior to cementing, irrigate the bone surfaces and drill sclerotic areas with a 1/8" drill bit to a depth of approximately
1/8". Firmly press bone cement into the bone surfaces, including the reamed keel entry hole to allow for adequate
indigitation. Place bone cement on the under surface of tibial definitive implant and firmly impact it on the prepared
tibia using the tibial impactor. Remove access bone cement.
Hyperflex the knee and dry the distal femoral bone cuts. Finger pressurise the posterior condyles with the bone cement.
Apply the bone cement to the under surface of the femoral component. Firmly impact the femoral component into place
using femoral impactor. Remove access bone cement.
If the metal backed tibial tray is being used, irrigate the surface of the tray and remove any access debris to clear the
locking mechanism. Firmly impact the selected articular surface liner into place and check to see that the locking
mechanism is engaged.
Reduce the knee and place it into extension. Evert the patella, dry the bony surface of patella and place bone cement
into the bone surface, apply bone cement underneath the patella implant. Place the patella implant on the resected
bone. Use patella pressuriser clamp to secure the patella implant. Trim access osteophytes and remove access bone
cement.

full_raw_transcription:
ARTHROSCOPY & SPORTS MEDICINE SOLUTIONS
“Unleash the potential”
Meril is a global medical device company... Cardiovascular | Orthopedics | Diagnostics | Endo-Surgery | Robotics | ENT

SHOULDER ARTHROSCOPY:
INSTAREP-TI (Titanium Anchor): Meril’s INSTAREP-TI Titanium Ligament Anchors... fixation in soft tissue repairs. Available in Multiple Sizes. USP #2 (UHMWPE) suture. High-Strength Titanium (Ti-6Al-4V Grade 5 ELI). Self-Drilling & Screw-in. Needled version available. Rotator Cuff, Bankart, SLAP Repair.
Ordering: MA-SZT00002 (Ø2mm w/ needle), MA-SZT00003 (Ø3mm w/o needle), MA-SZT00004 (Ø3mm w/ needle).

ROTAFIX TI (Headless Titanium Anchor): fully-threaded body, independent fiber channels. 4.5mm, 5.0mm, 5.5mm, 6.5mm diameters. USP #2 UHMWPE sutures. Advanced thread design for cancellous/osteoporotic bone.
Ordering: MA-SZT00016 (Ø6.5mm w/ needle), MA-SZT00017 (Ø5.5mm w/o needle), MA-SZT00014 (Ø5.5mm w/ needle), MA-SZT00011 (Ø4.5mm w/o needle), MA-SZT00007 (Ø5mm w/o needle).

INSTAREP BIO & ROTAFIX BIO (Bio-Composite Anchor): resorbable PLGA + β-TCP. Natural bone integration. Dual threads. 90-degree suture alignment.
Ordering: MA-SZB00001 (2.95x12mm), MA-SZB00004 (5.5x16mm Tape), MA-SZB00003 (5.5x16mm), MA-SZB00006 (6.5x16mm Tape).

INSTAREP PEEK (PEEK Anchor): Non-absorbable PEEK implant. 2.9mm diameter. Tap-in/Bang-on design.
Ordering: MA-SZP00001 (Ø2.9mm w/o needle).

ROTAFIX PEEK (Knotted Peek Anchor): 3.5mm & 5.5mm. Dual-thread. Footprint contact enhancement with tape suture.
Ordering: MA-SZP00005 (Ø5.5mm w/o needle), MA-SZP00012 (Ø3.5mm Tape w/ needle), MA-SZP00013 (Ø5.5mm Tape w/o needle), MA-SZP00018 (Ø3.5mm Cortical w/ needle).

FILAHOOK (All suture Soft Anchor): UHMWPE material. Minimal bone removal. 1.2mm, 1.5mm, 1.8mm, 2.9mm. Flexible driver available.
Ordering: MA-SZU00002 (1.2mm w/ needle), MA-SZU00004 (1.5mm w/ needle), MA-SZU00006 (1.8mm w/ needle), MA-SZU00007 (2.9mm w/o needle), MA-SZU00010 (2.9mm Tape w/ needle).

KNOTLESS ANCHORS:
ROTAFIX (PEEK+PEEK): 3.5mm, 5.0mm. Eyelet holds up to 8 sutures.
ROTAFIX (PEEK + TI): 5.0mm. Hybrid construct for double-row rotator cuff repair.

KNEE ARTHROSCOPY:
FEXIBUTTON (Adjustable Loop System): Titanium button (Ti-6Al-4V ELI). USP #5 UHMWPE pull rope. Intraoperatively customizable.
Ordering: MA-KZT00040 (70mm), MA-KOTFF110 (110mm #05), MA-KOTHH110 (110mm #07).

ENDOSTUD (Fixed Loop System): Non-adjustable. UTS exceeds 2200N.
Ordering: MA-KBT00010 (10mm) to MA-KBT00060 (60mm).

FERENCE-TI (Titanium Interference Screws): Ti-6Al-4V ELI. Blunt-tip design. 7mm to 12mm diameters. 20mm to 30mm lengths.
FERENCE-PEEK (PEEK Interference Screws): Medical-grade PEEK. MRI-compatible. Radiolucent.

BIO-FERENCE (PLGA+BETA TCP): Bio-composite, osteoconductive. 6x25mm to 11x30mm.
BIO-FERENCE (PLLA+HA): Bioabsorbable, supports bone regeneration.

MENISCAL REPAIR:
MENISCAL-DARN (Inside-Out): Flexible needle, UHMWPE sutures.
RAPID-FIX (All-Inside): PEEK anchors, ergonomic single-handed design. Access to all zones.

EQUIPMENTS & INSTRUMENTATION:
PERSIST Medical Trolley: Alluminum alloy, 128.4cm height, universal silent wheels.
PERSIST LED Cold Light Source: 80W, 2000lm, 5000k-7000k.
PERSIST 32 Inch 4K/HD Medical Monitor: 3840X2160 (4K), 1920X1080 (HD). 1200:1 contrast.
4K UHD Endoscope (built-in LED): 8.4M pixels, 1800 lines resolution, IPX-8.
PERSIST Shaver System: 1000-5000 RPM (Oscillation), 6000 RPM (Linear). Touch screen.
PERSIST RF System: Spinuss RF Console, 40-70℃ low temp ablation. 220W max.

Shoulder Instrumentation: TrustPass Suture Passer, Suture Cutter, Clever Hook, Sixter, etc. (MA-INDTSH001 to MA-INDTSH055).
Knee Instrumentation: Femoral Reamer, Tibial Reamer, Tendon Stripper, ACL/PCL Aimer, etc. (MA-INDTKN001 to MA-INDTKN127).

Footer: Meril Healthcare Pvt. Ltd. First Floor, H1 - H3, Meril Park, Vapi - 396191, Gujarat, India. M.L.NO. MFG/MD/2018/000063. contact: spm@merillife.com

MERIL CLAVO™ INTRAMEDULLARY NAILING SYSTEM
PFRN - PROXIMAL FEMORAL ROTATIONAL STABILITY NAIL

MANUFACTURING FACILITY: Vapi, Gujarat, India.
MERIL ACADEMY: World class state-of-the-art Training & Education centre.

MANUFACTURER:
Meril Healthcare Pvt. Ltd.
Ground & First Floor, Survey No. 173/4 & First Floor, H1-H3, Meril Park,
Survey No. 135/2/B & 174/2, Muktanand Marg, Chala, Vapi - 396 191, Gujarat, India.
Tel: +91 (260) 305 2100 | Email: askinfo@merilife.com | www.merillife.com

PRODUCT DESCRIPTION:
Anatomical Design for the best fit in the Femur bone.
* M/L angle of 5 degree allows easy insertion.
* Bendable tip reduces Stress on the bone.
* Proximal design for rotational stability.

INDICATIONS:

full_raw_transcription:
INFECTION PREVENTION SOLUTIONS 
The Power to Eliminate
The Promise to Protect
ZERO COMPROMISE Disinfection & Sterilization 
Isopropyl Alcohol IP – 70% Solution
Effective Surface Disinfection & Equipment Cleaning
Composition: MIREY 70% IPA - Isopropyl Alcohol IP – 70%.
Key Properties: Ready-to-use disinfectant, Rapid Evaporation, For Electronic Equipment.
Usage Instructions:
For Electronic Equipment: Spray MIREY 70% IPA onto a sterile gauze to moisten it. Do not spray directly on screens or sensitive electronic equipment. Wipe the screen or surface gently in one direction only to avoid streaks and static damage.
For Surface: Wipe the surface to physically remove any contaminants. Spray from a distance of 6–8 inches on surface. Apply directly onto surfaces ensuring even coverage. Keep surfaces visibly wet for effective disinfection. Always close the nozzle after use.
Precaution: Avoid use on alcohol-sensitive materials such as acrylic glass.
Pack Size: 250ml (Bottle/Carton: 20 Bottles).
Upcoming Product Range:
1. Inviro: Alcohol based Surface and Equipment Disinfectant. Each 100 gms contains Ethanol (Denatured) 10 gms, 2-Propanol - 9 gms, 1-Propanol - 6 gms.
2. Inviro Pro: Aldehyde free 4th generation QAC Surface Disinfectant Concentrate with perfume. Each 100 gms contains Didecyldimethyl ammonium chloride 7 gms, Perfume.
3. Inviro: Aldehyde free 4th generation QAC Surface Disinfectant Concentrate. Surface cleaner/ disinfectant. Each 100 gms contains Didecyldimethyl ammonium chloride - 7 gms.
4. Myscan: 2.45% Glutaraldehyde. Instrument & Scope Disinfectant. Glutaraldehyde Solution 2.45% w/v.
5. Myscan: 2% Glutaraldehyde. Instrument & Scope Disinfectant. Glutaraldehyde Solution 2%.
6. Myscan OPA: Orthophathaldehyde -0.55%, Colour- Alzarine Cynine Green F.
7. Mynox: Hospital Fabric & Linen Disinfectant. Didecyldimethyl ammonium Chloride, Citric acid, Ortho-Phosphoric acid, Enzyme, Fragrance, Purified water.

For Electronic Equipment: Spray MIREY 70% IPA onto a sterile gauze to moisten it. Do not spray directly on screens or sensitive electronic equipment. Wipe the screen or surface gently in one direction only to avoid streaks and static damage.

INFECTION PREVENTION SOLUTIONS

The Promise to Protect
ZERO COMPROMISE Disinfection & Sterilization 
Isopropyl Alcohol IP – 70% Solution
Effective Surface Disinfection & Equipment Cleaning
Composition: MIREY 70% IPA - Isopropyl Alcohol IP – 70%.
Key Properties: Ready-to-use disinfectant, Rapid Evaporation, For Electronic Equipment.
Usage Instructions:
For Electronic Equipment: Spray MIREY 70% IPA onto a sterile gauze to moisten it. Do not spray directly on screens or sensitive electronic equipment. Wipe the screen or surface gently in one direction only to avoid streaks and static damage.
For Surface: Wipe the surface to physically remove any contaminants. Spray from a distance of 6–8 inches on surface. Apply directly onto surfaces ensuring even coverage. Keep surfaces visibly wet for effective disinfection. Always close the nozzle after use.
Precaution: Avoid use on alcohol-sensitive materials such as acrylic glass.
Pack Size: 250ml (Bottle/Carton: 20 Bottles).

“Unleash the potential”

SHOULDER ARTHROSCOPY:
INSTAREP-TI (Titanium Anchor): Meril’s INSTAREP-TI Titanium Ligament Anchors... fixation in soft tissue repairs. Available in Multiple Sizes. USP #2 (UHMWPE) suture. High-Strength Titanium (Ti-6Al-4V Grade 5 ELI). Self-Drilling & Screw-in. Needled version available. Rotator Cuff, Bankart, SLAP Repair.
Ordering: MA-SZT00002 (Ø2mm w/ needle), MA-SZT00003 (Ø3mm w/o needle), MA-SZT00004 (Ø3mm w/ needle).

ROTAFIX TI (Headless Titanium Anchor): fully-threaded body, independent fiber channels. 4.5mm, 5.0mm, 5.5mm, 6.5mm diameters. USP #2 UHMWPE sutures. Advanced thread design for cancellous/osteoporotic bone.
Ordering: MA-SZT00016 (Ø6.5mm w/ needle), MA-SZT00017 (Ø5.5mm w/o needle), MA-SZT00014 (Ø5.5mm w/ needle), MA-SZT00011 (Ø4.5mm w/o needle), MA-SZT00007 (Ø5mm w/o needle).

INSTAREP BIO & ROTAFIX BIO (Bio-Composite Anchor): resorbable PLGA + β-TCP. Natural bone integration. Dual threads. 90-degree suture alignment.
Ordering: MA-SZB00001 (2.95x12mm), MA-SZB00004 (5.5x16mm Tape), MA-SZB00003 (5.5x16mm), MA-SZB00006 (6.5x16mm Tape).

INSTAREP PEEK (PEEK Anchor): Non-absorbable PEEK implant. 2.9mm diameter. Tap-in/Bang-on design.
Ordering: MA-SZP00001 (Ø2.9mm w/o needle).

ROTAFIX PEEK (Knotted Peek Anchor): 3.5mm & 5.5mm. Dual-thread. Footprint contact enhancement with tape suture.
Ordering: MA-SZP00005 (Ø5.5mm w/o needle), MA-SZP00012 (Ø3.5mm Tape w/ needle), MA-SZP00013 (Ø5.5mm Tape w/o needle), MA-SZP00018 (Ø3.5mm Cortical w/ needle).

FILAHOOK (All suture Soft Anchor): UHMWPE material. Minimal bone removal. 1.2mm, 1.5mm, 1.8mm, 2.9mm. Flexible driver available.
Ordering: MA-SZU00002 (1.2mm w/ needle), MA-SZU00004 (1.5mm w/ needle), MA-SZU00006 (1.8mm w/ needle), MA-SZU00007 (2.9mm w/o needle), MA-SZU00010 (2.9mm Tape w/ needle).

KNOTLESS ANCHORS:
ROTAFIX (PEEK+PEEK): 3.5mm, 5.0mm. Eyelet holds up to 8 sutures.
ROTAFIX (PEEK + TI): 5.0mm. Hybrid construct for double-row rotator cuff repair.

KNEE ARTHROSCOPY:
FEXIBUTTON (Adjustable Loop System): Titanium button (Ti-6Al-4V ELI). USP #5 UHMWPE pull rope. Intraoperatively customizable.
Ordering: MA-KZT00040 (70mm), MA-KOTFF110 (110mm #05), MA-KOTHH110 (110mm #07).

ENDOSTUD (Fixed Loop System): Non-adjustable. UTS exceeds 2200N.
Ordering: MA-KBT00010 (10mm) to MA-KBT00060 (60mm).

FERENCE-TI (Titanium Interference Screws): Ti-6Al-4V ELI. Blunt-tip design. 7mm to 12mm diameters. 20mm to 30mm lengths.
FERENCE-PEEK (PEEK Interference Screws): Medical-grade PEEK. MRI-compatible. Radiolucent.

BIO-FERENCE (PLGA+BETA TCP): Bio-composite, osteoconductive. 6x25mm to 11x30mm.
BIO-FERENCE (PLLA+HA): Bioabsorbable, supports bone regeneration.

MENISCAL REPAIR:
MENISCAL-DARN (Inside-Out): Flexible needle, UHMWPE sutures.
RAPID-FIX (All-Inside): PEEK anchors, ergonomic single-handed design. Access to all zones.

EQUIPMENTS & INSTRUMENTATION:
PERSIST Medical Trolley: Alluminum alloy, 128.4cm height, universal silent wheels.
PERSIST LED Cold Light Source: 80W, 2000lm, 5000k-7000k.
PERSIST 32 Inch 4K/HD Medical Monitor: 3840X2160 (4K), 1920X1080 (HD). 1200:1 contrast.
4K UHD Endoscope (built-in LED): 8.4M pixels, 1800 lines resolution, IPX-8.
PERSIST Shaver System: 1000-5000 RPM (Oscillation), 6000 RPM (Linear). Touch screen.
PERSIST RF System: Spinuss RF Console, 40-70℃ low temp ablation. 220W max.

Shoulder Instrumentation: TrustPass Suture Passer, Suture Cutter, Clever Hook, Sixter, etc. (MA-INDTSH001 to MA-INDTSH055).
Knee Instrumentation: Femoral Reamer, Tibial Reamer, Tendon Stripper, ACL/PCL Aimer, etc. (MA-INDTKN001 to MA-INDTKN127).

Footer: Meril Healthcare Pvt. Ltd. First Floor, H1 - H3, Meril Park, Vapi - 396191, Gujarat, India. M.L.NO. MFG/MD/2018/000063. contact: spm@merillife.com

full_raw_transcription:
UROLOGY SOLUTIONS
The Next Era Of Meril. Operational since 2007... dedicating to design and development of state-of-the-art devices.
Structural Heart, Orthopedics, Robotics, Endo-Surgery, ENT, IVD, Urology, Gastroenterology, Women's Healthcare, 360° Infection Prevention.

01. CONSUMABLES:
Ureteral Balloon Dilatation Catheter: Dual markers for precise balloon positioning. Rapid inflation/deflation. Pebax Material.
Size Matrix: 4 FR (60mm/850mm), 4 FR (60mm/650mm), 5 FR.
Use: Dilates ureteral strictures or prepares ureter for procedures.

Suprapubic Cystostomy Catheter: Chrysanthemum tip design prevents slip. Handle design for easy grip. Silicone remains soft at body temperature.
Use: Provides bladder drainage via percutaneous malecot catheter placement.

General-Purpose Ureteral Catheter: Soft PVC for flexibility. Tapered tip reduces trauma.
Use: Smooth navigation and precise contrast delivery.

Urinary Stone Retrieval Basket (Flexible & Rigid): Shape-memory design returns to original shape. Tipless basket reduces trauma. Nitinol wires. PI core for rotation control.
Size (Flexible): 1.7 FR, 1.9 FR, 2.2 FR, 3 FR. Length: 90cm, 110cm, 120cm.
Size (Rigid): 4.5 FR, Length: 55cm.
Use: Removes urinary stones during endoscopic procedures.

Urological Retrieval Coil: Secure extraction of stone pieces. Resists holmium laser energy. 3 FR x 15cm.
Use: Capture and remove urinary tract stones and objects.

Ureteral Access Sheath: Hydrophilic coating. Multiple scope entries without re-dilation. Lumen integrity.
Size Matrix: 9/11 FR, 10/12 FR, 9.5/11.5 FR, 10.5/12.5 FR, 12/14 FR. Lengths: 26cm, 35cm, 45cm.
Y-Type & YB Bend Sheaths: Continuous irrigation, simultaneous scope access and suction. 13/15 FR x 46cm available.

Amplatz Sheath: Tapered distal end for smooth advancement. Kink-resistant PTFE material.
Use: Dilates tissue around a dilator to maintain a nephrostomy tract.

Ureteral Stents: Temperature-controlled polyurethane (softens once inserted). Multiple holes/large lumens. Hydrophilic or non-hydrophilic.
Size Matrix: 4.8 FR, 5 FR, 6 FR. Lengths: 26cm, 28cm.
Mono Stent: Pigtail tip to retain in renal pelvis. 10 FR x 50cm.

Guidewires:
Zebra Guidewire: Nitinol core, white/blue stripes for visualization. 0.028 to 0.038 inch. Straight/Angled. 150cm to 450cm.
Hybrid Guidewire: Hydrophilic and PTFE coating.
Hydrotip Guidewire: PU distal tip (fluoroscopic visible).
Hydrophilic Guidewire: Ultra-low friction in wet conditions.
PTFE Guidewire: Flexible tip, excellent torquability.

Dilators:
Fascial Dilator Set: Smooth surface for atraumatic entry.
Urethral Dilator: 8FR to 24FR x 37cm.
Ureteral Dilator: 6FR to 16FR x 60cm.

Digital Flexible Ureteroscope: 6.3 FR, 7.5 FR, 8.5 FR. Apex bends 275° up/down, 90° left/right. FHD CMOS.
Image Processor: 3.2M pixels FHD. 100W LED. 3.0m cable.

Laser:
MeriFRAG + 40W Holmium Laser: 2100nm wavelength. 0.3-0.4mm penetration.
Technical: 40 Watts, 1-30Hz, 0.1-6.0J.
Modes: Fragmentation, Popcorn, Dusting. Reusable fibers (200-1000um).

PCNL Package: Includes Fascial Dilator Set, PTFE/Hydrophilic Guidewire, Puncture Needle (18G), Peel Away Sheath (12-18 FR), Nephrostomy Tube (12-20 FR).

SHOULDER ARTHROSCOPY:
INSTAREP-TI (Titanium Anchor): Meril’s INSTAREP-TI Titanium Ligament Anchors... fixation in soft tissue repairs. Available in Multiple Sizes. USP #2 (UHMWPE) suture. High-Strength Titanium (Ti-6Al-4V Grade 5 ELI). Self-Drilling & Screw-in. Needled version available. Rotator Cuff, Bankart, SLAP Repair.
Ordering: MA-SZT00002 (Ø2mm w/ needle), MA-SZT00003 (Ø3mm w/o needle), MA-SZT00004 (Ø3mm w/ needle).

ROTAFIX TI (Headless Titanium Anchor): fully-threaded body, independent fiber channels. 4.5mm, 5.0mm, 5.5mm, 6.5mm diameters. USP #2 UHMWPE sutures. Advanced thread design for cancellous/osteoporotic bone.
Ordering: MA-SZT00016 (Ø6.5mm w/ needle), MA-SZT00017 (Ø5.5mm w/o needle), MA-SZT00014 (Ø5.5mm w/ needle), MA-SZT00011 (Ø4.5mm w/o needle), MA-SZT00007 (Ø5mm w/o needle).

INSTAREP BIO & ROTAFIX BIO (Bio-Composite Anchor): resorbable PLGA + β-TCP. Natural bone integration. Dual threads. 90-degree suture alignment.
Ordering: MA-SZB00001 (2.95x12mm), MA-SZB00004 (5.5x16mm Tape), MA-SZB00003 (5.5x16mm), MA-SZB00006 (6.5x16mm Tape).

INSTAREP PEEK (PEEK Anchor): Non-absorbable PEEK implant. 2.9mm diameter. Tap-in/Bang-on design.
Ordering: MA-SZP00001 (Ø2.9mm w/o needle).

ROTAFIX PEEK (Knotted Peek Anchor): 3.5mm & 5.5mm. Dual-thread. Footprint contact enhancement with tape suture.
Ordering: MA-SZP00005 (Ø5.5mm w/o needle), MA-SZP00012 (Ø3.5mm Tape w/ needle), MA-SZP00013 (Ø5.5mm Tape w/o needle), MA-SZP00018 (Ø3.5mm Cortical w/ needle).

FILAHOOK (All suture Soft Anchor): UHMWPE material. Minimal bone removal. 1.2mm, 1.5mm, 1.8mm, 2.9mm. Flexible driver available.
Ordering: MA-SZU00002 (1.2mm w/ needle), MA-SZU00004 (1.5mm w/ needle), MA-SZU00006 (1.8mm w/ needle), MA-SZU00007 (2.9mm w/o needle), MA-SZU00010 (2.9mm Tape w/ needle).

KNOTLESS ANCHORS:
ROTAFIX (PEEK+PEEK): 3.5mm, 5.0mm. Eyelet holds up to 8 sutures.
ROTAFIX (PEEK + TI): 5.0mm. Hybrid construct for double-row rotator cuff repair.

KNEE ARTHROSCOPY:
FEXIBUTTON (Adjustable Loop System): Titanium button (Ti-6Al-4V ELI). USP #5 UHMWPE pull rope. Intraoperatively customizable.
Ordering: MA-KZT00040 (70mm), MA-KOTFF110 (110mm #05), MA-KOTHH110 (110mm #07).

ENDOSTUD (Fixed Loop System): Non-adjustable. UTS exceeds 2200N.
Ordering: MA-KBT00010 (10mm) to MA-KBT00060 (60mm).

FERENCE-TI (Titanium Interference Screws): Ti-6Al-4V ELI. Blunt-tip design. 7mm to 12mm diameters. 20mm to 30mm lengths.
FERENCE-PEEK (PEEK Interference Screws): Medical-grade PEEK. MRI-compatible. Radiolucent.

BIO-FERENCE (PLGA+BETA TCP): Bio-composite, osteoconductive. 6x25mm to 11x30mm.
BIO-FERENCE (PLLA+HA): Bioabsorbable, supports bone regeneration.

MENISCAL REPAIR:
MENISCAL-DARN (Inside-Out): Flexible needle, UHMWPE sutures.
RAPID-FIX (All-Inside): PEEK anchors, ergonomic single-handed design. Access to all zones.

EQUIPMENTS & INSTRUMENTATION:
PERSIST Medical Trolley: Alluminum alloy, 128.4cm height, universal silent wheels.
PERSIST LED Cold Light Source: 80W, 2000lm, 5000k-7000k.
PERSIST 32 Inch 4K/HD Medical Monitor: 3840X2160 (4K), 1920X1080 (HD). 1200:1 contrast.
4K UHD Endoscope (built-in LED): 8.4M pixels, 1800 lines resolution, IPX-8.
PERSIST Shaver System: 1000-5000 RPM (Oscillation), 6000 RPM (Linear). Touch screen.
PERSIST RF System: Spinuss RF Console, 40-70℃ low temp ablation. 220W max.

Shoulder Instrumentation: TrustPass Suture Passer, Suture Cutter, Clever Hook, Sixter, etc. (MA-INDTSH001 to MA-INDTSH055).
Knee Instrumentation: Femoral Reamer, Tibial Reamer, Tendon Stripper, ACL/PCL Aimer, etc. (MA-INDTKN001 to MA-INDTKN127).

1. Consumables (Catheters, Baskets, Sheaths):
- Deflure™ Ureteral Balloon Dilatation Catheter: Pebax material for flexibility, dual markers for precise positioning, rapid inflation/deflation. Use: Stricture dilatation.
- SupraSure™ Suprapubic Cystostomy Catheter: Silicone material, chrysanthemum tip design (Malecot) to prevent slip, handle for easy grip. Use: Bladder drainage.
- Rescath™ General-Purpose Ureteral Catheter: Soft PVC, tapered tip to reduce trauma. Size: 3FR to 7FR.
- Ri-Catch™ / Ri-Catch+™ (Flexible/Rigid): Nitinol 4-wire tipless baskets with shape memory. Tipless design reduces trauma.
- Messtone™ Urological Retrieval Coil: Extraction of stone pieces, laser-resistant coil (3FR).
- Provure™ / Provure+ / Provure Pro™ (Access Sheaths): Hydrophilic coating, kink-resistant, bendable tip (Pro), Y-connector for suction (+).
- Glizer™ Amplatz Sheath: PTFE material, kink-resistant, tapered distal end (12FR to 30FR).

2. Stents & Guidewires:
- UretrixPro™ / Uretrix™ / Uretrix™+ (Hydrophilic): Polyurethane stents, temperature-softened, tapered tip, large lumens for drainage. 4.8FR to 6FR.
- RiMosten™ Mono Stent: Kink-resistant PU, pigtail tip, for drainage and irrigation.
- Zebcor™ Zebra Guidewire: White/blue striped for visualization, Nitinol core, tapered tip (0.028" to 0.038").
- Ribrid™ Hybrid Guidewire: Hydrophilic and PTFE coating combo for effortless navigation.
- Xcursion Hydrotip™: Blue/white striped, PU distal tip (fluoroscopic visible), PTFE jacket.
- Hydroease™ (Hydrophilic): Ultra-low friction in wet conditions, memory retention.
- Meriskate™ (PTFE): Flexible tip for atraumatic advancement, high torquability.

3. Dilators:
- Dilato™ Fascial Dilator Set: Smooth surface for atraumatic entry (8FR to 18FR).
- Dilatrix™ Urethral Dilator: Adapts to anatomical curves, biocompatible material.
- EasyDi™ Ureteral Dilator: Tapered end, outstanding resilience (6FR to 16FR).

4. Digital Imaging & Laser:
- ri-Uniview™ Digital Flexible Ureteroscope: 6.3Fr, 7.5Fr, 8.5Fr options. CMOS sensor, 275° up/down deflection, 140° FOV.
- riUroSnap™ Image Processor: 1920x1080 FHD, 1/2.8" CMOS, USB/SD recording, 100W LED lamp.
- MeriFRAG™+ Holmium Laser Portable System: 40W Ho:YAG laser (2100nm). Modes: Fragmentation, Popcorn, Dusting. Reusable fibers.

5. Special Category:
- ProNeph™ PCNL Package: Comprehensive set including puncture needle, fascial dilators, guidewire, peel-away sheath, and nephrostomy tube.

1. Shoulder Arthroscopy (Ligament Anchors):

- ROTAFIX-TI™ Headless Titanium Anchor: 4.5mm to 6.5mm. Advanced thread for cancellous/osteoporotic bone. Independent fiber channels.
- INSTAREP-BIO™ / ROTAFIX-BIO™: Bio-composite (PLGA + Beta-TCP). Gradual resorption and bone remodeling. Dual threads.

2. Knee Arthroscopy (Ligament Fixation):
- FLEXIBUTTON™ Adjustable Loop System: Titanium button (Ti-6Al-4V) + USP #5 UHMWPE loop. Intraoperatively customizable.
- ENDOSTUD™ Fixed Loop System: Stable non-adjustable fixation. Tensile strength > 2200N. Large button for cortical expansion.
- FERENCE-TI™ Titanium Interference Screw: Fully threaded blunt-tip to prevent graft laceration. 5mm to 12mm sizes.
- FERENCE-PEEK™ Interference Screw: Radiolucent/MRI-compatible. Revision-ability.
- BIO-FERENCE™ (Bio-Composite / Bio-Absorbable): PLGA+Beta-TCP or PLLA+HA. Osteoconductive properties.
- MENISCAL DARN™ (Inside-Out): UHMWPE sutures for complex tears. Flexible needle design.
- RAPID-FIX™ (All-Inside): Minimally invasive, needle-shrouded system, PEEK anchors.

WBC Histogram Alarm
When WBC histogram is abnormal, alarming words "R1, R2, R3, R4, Rm" etc. are displayed.
R1: Left area of the lymphocyte peak is abnormal, there may be platelet clot, giant platelet,
nucleated red blood cell, undissolved red cell, protein & lipid particle or electric noise interference.
R2: The area between the lymphocyte peak and the middle cell is abnormal, there may be atypical
lymphocyte, plasmacyte, atypical lymphocyte, myeloblast or eosinophilia or basophilia.
R3: The area between the middle cell area and the neutrophil granulocyte peak may be abnormal,
there may be unmatured neutrophil granulocyte, abnormal cell subgroup or eosinophilia.
R4: The right area of the neutrophil granulocyte peak is abnormal, indicating that the absolute
neutrophil count increases.
Rm: Means there are two or more R alarms.
PLT Histogram Alarm
When PLT histogram is abnormal, alarming words "Pm" will be displayed.
Pm: the boundary between the platelet and the red cell area is vague, there may be giant platelet,
platelet clot, microcyte, cell debris and fibrous protein.

full_raw_transcription:
MERIL DIAGNOSTICS - CLIN QUANT MICRO / MERILYZER
BIOCHEMISTRY SEMI-AUTO ANALYZER

MANUFACTURER:
Meril Diagnostics Pvt. Ltd.
D1-D3, Second Floor, Meril Park, Muktanand Marg, Chala, Vapi - 396 191, Gujarat, India.
T: +91 260 240 8000 | E: diagnostics@merillife.com | www.merillife.com

TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS (MICRO):
- Assay Types/Modes: 8 modes (Absorbance, End Point, Fixed Time, Rate, Sample Blank, Multi Standard, Two point Non Linear, and Sample Blank Non Linear)
- Sample Type: Serum / Urine / Plasma / Body Fluids / Hemolysate
- Light Source: 6V, 10W Quartz Halogen Lamp (Life Span approx 2000 Hours)
- Measurement Method: Monochromatic and Bichromatic
- Photodiodes: Silicon photodiode
- Wavelength: Filter wheel with 6 Filters (340, 405, 505, 546, 578, 620 nm) and 2 Free positions (Total 8 positions)
- Absorbance Range: 0-3 Abs
- Resolution: 0.0001
- Types of Test ware: Quartz Flowcell
- Flowcell Volume: 32 µL
- Display: 240 x 128 pixel blue color graphical LCD with LED backlight
- PC Communication: 9 pin D type Serial Connector
- PC Software: Optional
- Memory: FLASH
- Storage: 25,600 Test Data Storage, 3 Month QC Data
- Quality Controls: Daily and Monthly for 3 levels with L-J Graph
- Air Aspiration Volume: Variable 0 to 50 µL (To reduce Carry over & Cross contamination)
- Cross Contamination: <1%
- Temperature Control: 25°C, 30°C, 37°C. Accuracy ±0.1°C, Peltier control
- Operating Voltage: 230V, 50 Hz, 45 Watt max
- Dimensions: 245 (W) mm x 273 (D) mm x 299 (H) mm
- Weight: ~10 kgs
- Key Pad: Mechanical / Touch key pad
- Calibration Type: Multi Point, Point to Point, Logit-Log, Spline, Polygonal curve, Linear factor, 1 point calibration, 2 point calibration

KEY FEATURES:
* 3 levels of QC with Levy Jennings plot

SICKLE CELL DISEASE
Types
There are many types of Sickle Cell Disease
(SCD), determined by the types of abnormal
hemoglobin (Hb) a person makes. Hb protein in
red blood cells carries oxygen from the lungs to
the rest of the body. People with SCD have
abnormal Hb, which doesn't carry oxygen well,
causing some of the medical problems of SCD.
The most common types of SCD are: HbSS, HbSC,
Hbs beta-Thalassemia, SCT or HbAS.
SYMPTOMS OF SICKLE CELL AΝΕΜΙΑ

HbSS
People with this type of SCD inherit a sickle cell gene ("S") from each parent. This is commonly called sickle
cell anemia.
HbSC
People with this type of SCD inherit a sickle cell gene ("S") from one parent and from the other parent a
gene for an abnormal Hb called "C".
HbS beta-thalassemia
People with this type of SCD inherit one sickle cell gene ("S") from one parent and one gene for beta-
thalassemia, another type of anemia, from the other parent. There are two types of beta-thalassemia:
"zero" and "plus".
Sickle Cell Trait (SCT or HbAS)
People with sickle cell trait inherit one sickle cell gene ("S") from one parent and one normal gene ("A") from the
other parent. People with SCT usually don't have signs of the disease and live a normal life, but they can pass
the sickle cell gene on to their children. However, SCT is not a mild form of sickle cell disease.

ROTAFIX TI
ROTAFIX-TI Titanium Ligament Anchors are designed for strength, reliability, and optimal surgical efficiency—
empowering surgeons with confidence in every fixation.
Available in Multiple Sizes – Offered in 4.5mm, 5.0mm, 5.5mm, and 6.5mm diameters, preloaded with USP #2 ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) sutures for secure fixation.

Advanced Thread Design – Features a cancellous thread with a small core diameter, maximizing pull-out strength, especially in cancellous and osteoporotic bone.
Enhanced Fixation Strength – Fully-threaded anchor body provides superior resistance to pull-out, ensuring long-term stability.
Multi-Suture & Tape Options – Available with two or three USP #2 sutures and contrasting-colored fiber tapes, improving suture identification and soft tissue fixation.
Independent Fiber Channels – Prevents suture binding, allowing smoother handling and improved surgical precision.
